sanskrit: tvam a̍gne pratha̱mo aṅgi̍rā̱ ṛṣi̍r de̱vo de̱vānā̍m abhavaḥ śi̱vaḥ sakhā̍ | tava̍ vra̱te ka̱vayo̍ vidma̱nāpa̱so 'jā̍yanta ma̱ruto̱ bhrāja̍dṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: You, O Agni, became the first among the Aṅgirases — a seer, a god, an auspicious friend of the gods. In your ordinance the poets, skillful in sacred knowledge, were born — the Maruts with gleaming spears.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne pratha̱mo aṅgi̍rastamaḥ ka̱vir de̱vānā̱m pari̍ bhūṣasi vra̱tam | vi̱bhur viśva̍smai̱ bhuva̍nāya̱ medhi̍ro dvimā̱tā śa̱yuḥ ka̍ti̱dhā ci̍d ā̱yave̍ ||
english: You, O Agni, most foremost of the Aṅgirases, as a seer you adorn the ordinance of the gods. All-pervading, wise for all the worlds, born of two mothers, you rest in many ways for man's benefit.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne pratha̱mo mā̍ta̱riśva̍na ā̱vir bha̍va sukratū̱yā vi̱vasva̍te | are̍jetā̱ṁ roda̍sī hotṛ̱vūrye 'sa̍ghnor bhā̱ram aya̍jo ma̱ho va̍so ||
english: You, O Agni, were first revealed by Mātariśvan to Vivasvat through your power of right action. Heaven and Earth trembled at the heroic deed of the Hotṛ; great One, you bore the burden [of sacrifice] and duly worshipped.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne̱ mana̍ve̱ dyām a̍vāśayaḥ purū̱rava̍se su̱kṛte̍ su̱kṛtta̍raḥ | śvā̱treṇa̱ yat pi̱tror mucya̍se̱ pary ā tvā̱ pūrva̍m anaya̱nn āpa̍ra̱m puna̍ḥ ||
english: You, O Agni, made heaven resound for Manu; for righteous Purūravas you were even more beneficent. When by a dog's [Śyāva's] means you were taken away from your parents, they brought you forth first and then again a second time.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne vṛṣa̱bhaḥ pu̍ṣṭi̱vardha̍na̱ udya̍tasruce bhavasi śra̱vāyya̍ḥ | ya āhu̍ti̱m pari̱ vedā̱ vaṣa̍ṭkṛti̱m ekā̍yu̱r agre̱ viśa̍ ā̱vivā̍sasi ||
english: You, O Agni, are the bull who increases nourishment; you become praiseworthy for him who lifts the ladle. As the sole life-force you who know the oblation and the vaṣaṭ-call attend upon the clans at the head.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne vṛji̱nava̍rtani̱ṁ nara̱ṁ sakma̍n piparṣi vi̱dathe̍ vicarṣaṇe | yaḥ śūra̍sātā̱ pari̍takmye̱ dhane̍ da̱bhrebhi̍ś ci̱t samṛ̍tā̱ haṁsi̱ bhūya̍saḥ ||
english: You, O Agni, on the crooked path carry the man [safely] in your company, all-seeing one, at the assembly. He who, in a contest of heroes, in a contest for stakes, slays even many arrayed opponents with [his] few.

sanskrit: tvaṁ tam a̍gne amṛta̱tva u̍tta̱me marta̍ṁ dadhāsi̱ śrava̍se di̱ve-di̍ve | yas tā̍tṛṣā̱ṇa u̱bhayā̍ya̱ janma̍ne̱ maya̍ḥ kṛ̱ṇoṣi̱ praya̱ ā ca̍ sū̱raye̍ ||
english: You, O Agni, establish that mortal man in the highest immortality for fame day by day — him who striving for both worlds you gladden, O Agni, and give refreshment to the pious one.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no̍ agne sa̱naye̱ dhanā̍nāṁ ya̱śasa̍ṁ kā̱ruṁ kṛ̍ṇuhi̱ stavā̍naḥ | ṛ̱dhyāma̱ karmā̱pasā̱ nave̍na de̱vair dyā̍vāpṛthivī̱ prāva̍taṁ naḥ ||
english: O Agni, being praised, make our singer renowned for the winning of wealth. May we prosper through new action and work; may Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no̍ agne pi̱tror u̱pastha̱ ā de̱vo de̱veṣv a̍navadya̱ jāgṛ̍viḥ | ta̱nū̱kṛd bo̍dhi̱ prama̍tiś ca kā̱rave̱ tvaṁ ka̍lyāṇa̱ vasu̱ viśva̱m opi̍ṣe ||
english: You, O Agni, in the lap of our parents, a god blameless among the gods, keep vigil. Be the body-fashioner and the guiding wisdom for the singer; you, O auspicious one, protect all good wealth.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne̱ prama̍ti̱s tvam pi̱tāsi̍ na̱s tvaṁ va̍ya̱skṛt tava̍ jā̱mayo̍ va̱yam | saṁ tvā̱ rāya̍ḥ śa̱tina̱ḥ saṁ sa̍ha̱sriṇa̍ḥ su̱vīra̍ṁ yanti vrata̱pām a̍dābhya ||
english: O Agni, you are our guiding wisdom, you are our father; you are the maker of [our] strength — we are your kindred. May hundreds of riches, may thousands flow to you together, O guardian of ordinances, undeceivable one, along with brave heroes.

sanskrit: tvām a̍gne pratha̱mam ā̱yum ā̱yave̍ de̱vā a̍kṛṇva̱n nahu̍ṣasya vi̱śpati̍m | iḻā̍m akṛṇva̱n manu̍ṣasya̱ śāsa̍nīm pi̱tur yat pu̱tro mama̍kasya̱ jāya̍te ||
english: You, O Agni, the gods made the first living one for Āyu, the lord of the clan of Nahuṣa. They made Iḷā as the instructor of human beings, as when a son is born to his own father.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no̍ agne̱ tava̍ deva pā̱yubhi̍r ma̱ghono̍ rakṣa ta̱nva̍ś ca vandya | trā̱tā to̱kasya̱ tana̍ye̱ gavā̍m a̱sy ani̍meṣa̱ṁ rakṣa̍māṇa̱s tava̍ vra̱te ||
english: O Agni, O god worthy of homage, protect the magnanimous man and his body with your watchers. You are the protector of offspring and of progeny with cattle, guarding without blinking, within your ordinance.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne̱ yajya̍ve pā̱yur anta̍ro 'niṣa̱ṅgāya̍ catura̱kṣa i̍dhyase | yo rā̱taha̍vyo 'vṛ̱kāya̱ dhāya̍se kī̱reś ci̱n mantra̱m mana̍sā va̱noṣi̱ tam ||
english: You, O Agni, four-eyed one, are kindled as the inner guardian for the worshipper who is free from injury. You who are invoked with oblations tend the wolf-free one; even the bard's prayer you gain by mind.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gna uru̱śaṁsā̍ya vā̱ghate̍ spā̱rhaṁ yad rekṇa̍ḥ para̱maṁ va̱noṣi̱ tat | ā̱dhrasya̍ ci̱t prama̍tir ucyase pi̱tā pra pāka̱ṁ śāssi̱ pra diśo̍ vi̱duṣṭa̍raḥ ||
english: O Agni, for the widely praised singer you obtain that which is the most desirable supreme wealth. Even for the helpless one you are called the guiding wisdom and father; you instruct the simple, knowing the directions better than any.

sanskrit: tvam a̍gne̱ praya̍tadakṣiṇa̱ṁ nara̱ṁ varme̍va syū̱tam pari̍ pāsi vi̱śvata̍ḥ | svā̱du̱kṣadmā̱ yo va̍sa̱tau syo̍na̱kṛj jī̍vayā̱jaṁ yaja̍te̱ sopa̱mā di̱vaḥ ||
english: You, O Agni, protect from all sides the man who extends his right hand like one sewn in armour. He who eats sweet food, who makes a comfortable dwelling, who sacrifices the living sacrifice — he is the equal of heaven.

sanskrit: i̱mām a̍gne śa̱raṇi̍m mīmṛṣo na i̱mam adhvā̍na̱ṁ yam agā̍ma dū̱rāt | ā̱piḥ pi̱tā prama̍tiḥ so̱myānā̱m bhṛmi̍r asy ṛṣi̱kṛn martyā̍nām ||
english: Do not, O Agni, disregard this road of ours, this path along which we have come from afar. You are kinsman, father, and guide of the Soma-pressing ones; you are the active maker of seers among mortals.

sanskrit: ma̱nu̱ṣvad a̍gne aṅgira̱svad a̍ṅgiro yayāti̱vad sada̍ne pūrva̱vac chu̍ce | accha̍ yā̱hy ā va̍hā̱ daivya̱ṁ jana̱m ā sā̍daya ba̱rhiṣi̱ yakṣi̍ ca pri̱yam ||
english: O Agni, O Aṅgiras, as [you dwelt] with Manu, as with the Aṅgirases, as with Yayāti in the seat of old, O bright one — come hither, bring the divine folk, seat them on the sacred grass, and worship what is dear.

sanskrit: e̱tenā̍gne̱ brahma̍ṇā vāvṛdhasva̱ śaktī̍ vā̱ yat te̍ cakṛ̱mā vi̱dā vā̍ | u̱ta pra ṇe̍ṣy a̱bhi vasyo̍ a̱smān saṁ na̍ḥ sṛja suma̱tyā vāja̍vatyā ||
english: O Agni, strengthen yourself with this sacred prayer, or with whatever power we have performed, or with wisdom. Also lead us forward to greater wealth; unite us with a well-disposed, vigorous thought.

sanskrit: indra̍sya̱ nu vī̱ryā̍ṇi̱ pra vo̍ca̱ṁ yāni̍ ca̱kāra̍ pratha̱māni̍ va̱jrī | aha̱nn ahi̱m anv a̱pas ta̍tarda̱ pra va̱kṣaṇā̍ abhina̱t parva̍tānām ||
english: Now I will proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra — the first deeds which the vajra-wielder performed. He slew the serpent [Vṛtra], and then he bored through the waters; he split open the bellies of the mountains.

sanskrit: aha̱nn ahi̱m parva̍te śiśriyā̱ṇaṁ tvaṣṭā̍smai̱ vajra̍ṁ sva̱rya̍ṁ tatakṣa | vā̱śrā i̍va dhe̱nava̱ḥ syanda̍mānā̱ añja̍ḥ samu̱dram ava̍ jagmu̱r āpa̍ḥ ||
english: He slew the serpent lying on the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the sky-roaring thunderbolt. Like lowing cows rushing swiftly, the waters flowed straight down to the ocean.

sanskrit: vṛ̱ṣā̱yamā̍ṇo 'vṛṇīta̱ soma̱ṁ trika̍drukeṣv apibat su̱tasya̍ | ā sāya̍kam ma̱ghavā̍datta̱ vajra̱m aha̍nn enam prathama̱jām ahī̍nām ||
english: Acting like a bull he chose Soma and drank of the pressed juice at the three Tri-kadrukas. Maghavan took up the lightning weapon, the missile, and slew Vṛtra, the first-born among serpents.

sanskrit: yad i̱ndrāha̍n prathama̱jām ahī̍nā̱m ān mā̱yinā̱m ami̍nā̱ḥ prota mā̱yāḥ | āt sūrya̍ṁ ja̱naya̱n dyām u̱ṣāsa̍ṁ tā̱dītnā̱ śatru̱ṁ na kilā̍ vivitse ||
english: When, O Indra, you slew the first-born of serpents and outwitted the māyā-tricks of the tricksters, generating the sun, the sky, and the dawn at that very moment — then indeed you found no enemy to withstand you.

sanskrit: aha̍n vṛ̱traṁ vṛ̍tra̱tara̱ṁ vya̍ṁsa̱m indro̱ vajre̍ṇa maha̱tā va̱dhena̍ | skandhā̍ṁsīva̱ kuli̍śenā̱ vivṛ̱kṇāhi̍ḥ śayata upa̱pṛk pṛ̍thi̱vyāḥ ||
english: Indra slew Vṛtra, the more formidable hinderer, with his great weapon, the thunderbolt. Like the trunk of a tree split by an axe, the serpent lay prostrate, touching the earth.

sanskrit: a̱yo̱ddheva̍ du̱rmada̱ ā hi ju̱hve ma̍hāvī̱raṁ tu̍vibā̱dham ṛ̍jī̱ṣam | nātā̍rīd asya̱ samṛ̍tiṁ va̱dhānā̱ṁ saṁ ru̱jānā̍ḥ pipiṣa̱ indra̍śatruḥ ||
english: Like a man drunk and unfit for battle, Vṛtra challenged the great hero, the mighty assailer, the soma-drinker. He did not withstand the onslaught of his weapons; shattered, with broken joints, lay Indra's enemy.

sanskrit: a̱pād a̍ha̱sto a̍pṛtanya̱d indra̱m āsya̱ vajra̱m adhi̱ sānau̍ jaghāna | vṛṣṇo̱ vadhri̍ḥ prati̱māna̱m bubhū̍ṣan puru̱trā vṛ̱tro a̍śaya̱d vya̍staḥ ||
english: Footless and handless, Vṛtra still fought against Indra; Indra smote him on the back with his thunderbolt. The castrated one, seeking to match the bull [Indra], lay shattered in many places.

sanskrit: na̱daṁ na bhi̱nnam a̍mu̱yā śayā̍na̱m mano̱ ruhā̍ṇā̱ ati̍ ya̱nty āpa̍ḥ | yāś ci̍d vṛ̱tro ma̍hi̱nā pa̱ryati̍ṣṭha̱t tāsā̱m ahi̍ḥ patsuta̱ḥśīr ba̍bhūva ||
english: Like a broken reed, Vṛtra lay there, and over him the waters flowed, riding on his mind [i.e. flooding his body]. Those [waters] which Vṛtra in his greatness had encompassed — the serpent now lay with his head at their feet.

sanskrit: nī̱cāva̍yā abhavad vṛ̱trapu̱trendro̍ asyā̱ ava̱ vadha̍r jabhāra | utta̍rā̱ sūr adha̍raḥ pu̱tra ā̍sī̱d dānu̍ḥ śaye sa̱hava̍tsā̱ na dhe̱nuḥ ||
english: Vṛtra's mother, Dānu, became one who sinks downward; Indra hurled his weapon upon her. Above lay the mother, below lay the son; Dānu lay there like a cow with her calf.

sanskrit: ati̍ṣṭhantīnām aniveśa̱nānā̱ṁ kāṣṭhā̍nā̱m madhye̱ nihi̍ta̱ṁ śarī̍ram | vṛ̱trasya̍ ni̱ṇyaṁ vi ca̍ra̱nty āpo̍ dī̱rghaṁ tama̱ āśa̍ya̱d indra̍śatruḥ ||
english: In the midst of the channels that stand motionless and never rest, the body of Vṛtra lay hid; the waters flow over his secret parts — Indra's enemy lay in long darkness.

sanskrit: dā̱sapa̍tnī̱r ahi̍gopā atiṣṭha̱n niru̍ddhā̱ āpa̍ḥ pa̱ṇine̍va̱ gāva̍ḥ | a̱pām bila̱m api̍hita̱ṁ yad āsī̍d vṛ̱traṁ ja̍gha̱nvām̐ apa̱ tad va̍vāra ||
english: The waters stood still, guarded by the Dāsa's rule, guarded by the serpent — dammed up like cows held by a Paṇi. When Indra had slain Vṛtra, he opened the blocked opening of the waters.

sanskrit: aśvyo̱ vāro̍ abhava̱s tad i̍ndra sṛ̱ke yat tvā̍ pra̱tyaha̍n de̱va eka̍ḥ | aja̍yo̱ gā aja̍yaḥ śūra̱ soma̱m avā̍sṛja̱ḥ sarta̍ve sa̱pta sindhū̍n ||
english: You became, O Indra, like a horse's tail at that moment when the one god [Vṛtra] struck back at you. You conquered the cattle, O hero, you conquered Soma; you released the seven rivers to flow.

sanskrit: nāsmai̍ vi̱dyun na ta̍nya̱tuḥ si̍ṣedha̱ na yām miha̱m aki̍rad dhrā̱duni̍ṁ ca | indra̍ś ca̱ yad yu̍yu̱dhāte̱ ahi̍ś co̱tāpa̱rībhyo̍ ma̱ghavā̱ vi ji̍gye ||
english: Neither lightning nor thunder could stop him; nor the mist he scattered, nor the hail. When Indra and the serpent fought, Maghavan indeed conquered, now and for the future.

sanskrit: ahe̍r yā̱tāra̱ṁ kam a̍paśya indra hṛ̱di yat te̍ ja̱ghnuṣo̱ bhīr aga̍cchat | nava̍ ca̱ yan na̍va̱tiṁ ca̱ srava̍ntīḥ śye̱no na bhī̱to ata̍ro̱ rajā̍ṁsi ||
english: Whom did you see as the avenger of the serpent, O Indra, when fear entered your heart after the slaying? Then like a frightened eagle you crossed the ninety-nine rivers.

sanskrit: indro̍ yā̱to 'va̍sitasya̱ rājā̱ śama̍sya ca śṛ̱ṅgiṇo̱ vajra̍bāhuḥ | sed u̱ rājā̍ kṣayati carṣaṇī̱nām a̱rān na ne̱miḥ pari̱ tā ba̍bhūva ||
english: Indra the king of that which is exhausted and of that which is quiet, the horned one, the vajra-armed — he indeed rules as king over all peoples. Like a wheel's rim he encircled them all.

sanskrit: etāyā̱mopa̍ ga̱vyanta̱ indra̍m a̱smāka̱ṁ su prama̍tiṁ vāvṛdhāti | a̱nā̱mṛ̱ṇaḥ ku̱vid ād a̱sya rā̱yo gavā̱ṁ keta̱m para̍m ā̱varja̍te naḥ ||
english: Let us go on this journey to Indra, seeking cattle; let him promote our good understanding. Unstricken by debts — will he now turn to us the innermost desire of his wealth of cattle?

sanskrit: uped a̱haṁ dha̍na̱dām apra̍tīta̱ṁ juṣṭā̱ṁ na śye̱no va̍sa̱tim pa̍tāmi | indra̍ṁ nama̱syann u̍pa̱mebhi̍r a̱rkair yaḥ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ havyo̱ asti̱ yāma̍n ||
english: I fly toward the unchallenged wealth-giver, toward a favorable abode, like a hawk. Reverencing Indra with my highest hymns — he who is invocable by singers along the way.

sanskrit: ni sarva̍sena iṣu̱dhīm̐r a̍sakta̱ sam a̱ryo gā a̍jati̱ yasya̱ vaṣṭi̍ | co̱ṣkū̱yamā̍ṇa indra̱ bhūri̍ vā̱mam mā pa̱ṇir bhū̍r a̱smad adhi̍ pravṛddha ||
english: The noble man whose quiver is stuck full [with arrows] drives together the cattle of whoever desires them. O Indra, you who roar aloud with abundant wealth — do not be a Paṇi, superior to us in might.

sanskrit: vadhī̱r hi dasyu̍ṁ dha̱nina̍ṁ gha̱nena̱m̐ eka̱ś cara̍nn upaśā̱kebhi̍r indra | dhano̱r adhi̍ viṣu̱ṇak te vy ā̍ya̱nn aya̍jvānaḥ sana̱kāḥ preti̍m īyuḥ ||
english: You slew the Dasyu who is rich in possessions, O Indra, roaming alone with your supporters. Spreading in different directions from your bow, the ancients who did not sacrifice went to their doom.

sanskrit: parā̍ cic chī̱rṣā va̍vṛju̱s ta i̱ndrāya̍jvāno̱ yajva̍bhi̱ḥ spardha̍mānāḥ | pra yad di̱vo ha̍rivaḥ sthātar ugra̱ nir a̍vra̱tām̐ a̍dhamo̱ roda̍syoḥ ||
english: Those non-sacrificers competing with sacrificers even turned their heads away — when, O Indra, steady driver of bay horses, terrible one, you pressed the lawless ones out from both worlds.

sanskrit: ayu̍yutsann anava̱dyasya̱ senā̱m ayā̍tayanta kṣi̱tayo̱ nava̍gvāḥ ||
english: They could not fight against the blameless one's army; the Navagva clans went over to the opposite side. Armed with bull-like weapons, the castrated ones, driven out, came advancing toward Indra from the streams.

sanskrit: tvam e̱tān ru̍da̱to jakṣa̍ta̱ś cāyo̍dhayo̱ raja̍sa indra pā̱re | avā̍daho di̱va ā dasyu̍m u̱ccā pra su̍nva̱taḥ stu̍va̱taḥ śaṁsa̍m āvaḥ ||
english: These weeping and shouting ones, O Indra, you fought beyond the dust of battle. You burned the Dasyu down from the high sky; you furthered the glory of those who press Soma and those who sing praises.

sanskrit: ca̱krā̱ṇāsa̍ḥ parī̱ṇaha̍m pṛthi̱vyā hira̍ṇyena ma̱ṇinā̱ śumbha̍mānāḥ | na hi̍nvā̱nāsa̍s titiru̱s ta indra̱m pari̱ spaśo̍ adadhā̱t sūrye̍ṇa ||
english: Adorning themselves with gold jewels [spanning] the girth of the earth, those who were not urging [the sacrifice] could not cross over Indra; he stationed his spies around them with the sun.

sanskrit: pari̱ yad i̍ndra̱ roda̍sī u̱bhe abu̍bhojīr mahi̱nā vi̱śvata̍ḥ sīm | ama̍nyamānām̐ a̱bhi manya̍mānai̱r nir bra̱hmabhi̍r adhamo̱ dasyu̍m indra ||
english: When, O Indra, you encompassed both worlds everywhere with your greatness — you thrust out the Dasyu with your sacred prayers, [the gods] who think clearly against those who think [wrongly], O Indra.

sanskrit: na ye di̱vaḥ pṛ̍thi̱vyā anta̍m ā̱pur na mā̱yābhi̍r dhana̱dām pa̱ryabhū̍van | yuja̱ṁ vajra̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bhaś ca̍kra̱ indro̱ nir jyoti̍ṣā̱ tama̍so̱ gā a̍dukṣat ||
english: They did not reach the end of sky or earth, nor did they surpass the wealth-giver with their māyā. Indra the bull made his thunderbolt his ally; with light he milked the cattle out of the darkness.

sanskrit: anu̍ sva̱dhām a̍kṣara̱nn āpo̍ a̱syāva̍rdhata̱ madhya̱ ā nā̱vyā̍nām | sa̱dhrī̱cīne̍na̱ mana̍sā̱ tam indra̱ oji̍ṣṭhena̱ hanma̍nāhann a̱bhi dyūn ||
english: The waters flowed according to his own nature; he grew in the midst of the rivers. With concentrated mind, O Indra, with your mightiest blow you struck the gambler down.

sanskrit: ny ā̍vidhyad ilī̱biśa̍sya dṛ̱ḻhā vi śṛ̱ṅgiṇa̍m abhina̱c chuṣṇa̱m indra̍ḥ | yāva̱t taro̍ maghava̱n yāva̱d ojo̱ vajre̍ṇa̱ śatru̍m avadhīḥ pṛta̱nyum ||
english: He pierced through the strongholds of Ilībiśa; Indra split open the horned Śuṣṇa. As far as your sharpness, O Maghavan, as far as your might — with the thunderbolt you slew the attacking enemy.

sanskrit: a̱bhi si̱dhmo a̍jigād asya̱ śatrū̱n vi ti̱gmena̍ vṛṣa̱bheṇā̱ puro̍ 'bhet | saṁ vajre̍ṇāsṛjad vṛ̱tram indra̱ḥ pra svām ma̱tim a̍tira̱c chāśa̍dānaḥ ||
english: His force swept over his enemies; with his sharp bull-might he broke open the strongholds. Indra drove Vṛtra at the thunderbolt, surpassing his own intention as he conquers.

sanskrit: āva̱ḥ kutsa̍m indra̱ yasmi̍ñ cā̱kan prāvo̱ yudhya̍ntaṁ vṛṣa̱bhaṁ daśa̍dyum | śa̱phacyu̍to re̱ṇur na̍kṣata̱ dyām uc chvai̍tre̱yo nṛ̍ṣāhyā̍ya tasthau ||
english: O Indra, you helped Kutsa in whom you took pleasure; you aided the fighting bull Daśadyu. The dust raised by hooves touched the sky; the son of Śvitra stood up for the defeat of enemies.

sanskrit: āva̱ḥ śama̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bhaṁ tugryā̍su kṣetraje̱ṣe ma̍ghava̱ñ chvitrya̱ṁ gām | jyok ci̱d atra̍ tasthi̱vāṁso̍ akrañ chatrūya̱tām adha̍rā̱ veda̍nākaḥ ||
english: O Maghavan, in the battle for fields you helped Śama the bull and Śvitryā the cow among the Tugryas. Even those who had stood here for long — the reward fell to those who acted as enemies.

sanskrit: triś ci̍n no a̱dyā bha̍vataṁ navedasā vi̱bhur vā̱ṁ yāma̍ u̱ta rā̱tir a̍śvinā | yu̱vor hi ya̱ntraṁ hi̱myeva̱ vāsa̍so 'bhyāya̱ṁsenyā̍ bhavatam manī̱ṣibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Be here with us three times today with new gifts, O Aśvins; your journey is vast and so is your bestowal. For your harnessing, like putting on a winter garment, should be eagerly done by the wise.

sanskrit: traya̍ḥ pa̱vayo̍ madhu̱vāha̍ne̱ rathe̱ soma̍sya ve̱nām anu̱ viśva̱ id vi̍duḥ | traya̍ḥ ska̱mbhāsa̍ḥ skabhi̱tāsa̍ ā̱rabhe̱ trir nakta̍ṁ yā̱thas trir v a̍śvinā̱ divā̍ ||
english: Three hubs are on the honey-bearing chariot in the wake of the Soma's longing — all know it. Three are the supports, set up to be grasped; three times by night you travel, O Aśvins, and three times by day.

sanskrit: sa̱mā̱ne aha̱n trir a̍vadyagohanā̱ trir a̱dya ya̱jñam madhu̍nā mimikṣatam | trir vāja̍vatī̱r iṣo̍ aśvinā yu̱vaṁ do̱ṣā a̱smabhya̍m u̱ṣasa̍ś ca pinvatam ||
english: On the same day, three times drive away blame; three times today fill the sacrifice with honey. Three times, O Aśvins, you two who have vigorous nourishment — fill us with bounty by night and at dawn.

sanskrit: trir va̱rtir yā̍ta̱ṁ trir anu̍vrate ja̱ne triḥ su̍prā̱vye̍ tre̱dheva̍ śikṣatam | trir nā̱ndya̍ṁ vahatam aśvinā yu̱vaṁ triḥ pṛkṣo̍ a̱sme a̱kṣare̍va pinvatam ||
english: Come three times for the oblation, three times to the obedient man; three times to the worthy one give succour, as if threefold. Three times bring the jubilation, O Aśvins; three times pour the nourishment into us like water through an axle.

sanskrit: trir no̍ ra̱yiṁ va̍hatam aśvinā yu̱vaṁ trir de̱vatā̍tā̱ trir u̱tāva̍ta̱ṁ dhiya̍ḥ | triḥ sau̍bhaga̱tvaṁ trir u̱ta śravā̍ṁsi nas tri̱ṣṭhaṁ vā̱ṁ sūre̍ duhi̱tā ru̍ha̱d ratha̍m ||
english: Three times bring us riches, O Aśvins you two; three times the divine favor, and three times support our thoughts. Three times good fortune and three times renown for us — may the sun's daughter mount your three-stepped chariot.

sanskrit: trir no̍ aśvinā di̱vyāni̍ bheṣa̱jā triḥ pārthi̍vāni̱ trir u̍ dattam a̱dbhyaḥ | o̱māna̍ṁ śa̱ṁyor mama̍kāya sū̱nave̍ tri̱dhātu̱ śarma̍ vahataṁ śubhas patī ||
english: Three times, O Aśvins, give us the heavenly medicines; three times the earthly, and three times those from the waters. Bring protection and well-being to my son who desires it — O lords of beauty, bring three-partite shelter.

sanskrit: trir no̍ aśvinā yaja̱tā di̱ve-di̍ve̱ pari̍ tri̱dhātu̍ pṛthi̱vīm a̍śāyatam | ti̱sro nā̍satyā rathyā parā̱vata̍ ā̱tmeva̱ vāta̱ḥ svasa̍rāṇi gacchatam ||
english: Three times a day, O Aśvins, worthy of worship, you two have lain around the earth with your three-partite resting. O Nāsatyas, you traverse three distant routes in your chariot, like the wind going to its own haunts.

sanskrit: trir a̍śvinā̱ sindhu̍bhiḥ sa̱ptamā̍tṛbhi̱s traya̍ āhā̱vās tre̱dhā ha̱viṣ kṛ̱tam | ti̱sraḥ pṛ̍thi̱vīr u̱pari̍ pra̱vā di̱vo nāka̍ṁ rakṣethe̱ dyubhi̍r a̱ktubhi̍r hi̱tam ||
english: Three times, O Aśvins, with the rivers of seven mothers; three invocations; the oblation prepared in three ways. You protect the three earths and the vault of heaven above the streams, fixed with days and nights.

sanskrit: kva1̱̍ trī ca̱krā tri̱vṛto̱ ratha̍sya̱ kva1̱̍ trayo̍ va̱ndhuro̱ ye sanī̍ḻāḥ | ka̱dā yogo̍ vā̱jino̱ rāsa̍bhasya̱ yena̍ ya̱jñaṁ nā̍satyopayā̱thaḥ ||
english: Where are the three wheels of the triple chariot? Where are the three yoke-poles that share a pole together? When is the yoking of the vigorous ass by which, O Nāsatyas, you come to the sacrifice?

sanskrit: ā nā̍satyā̱ gaccha̍taṁ hū̱yate̍ ha̱vir madhva̍ḥ pibatam madhu̱pebhi̍r ā̱sabhi̍ḥ | yu̱vor hi pūrva̍ṁ savi̱toṣaso̱ ratha̍m ṛ̱tāya̍ ci̱traṁ ghṛ̱tava̍nta̱m iṣya̍ti ||
english: Come here, O Nāsatyas — the oblation is being offered; drink of the honey with your honey-drinking lips. For Savitṛ first impels for Ṛta the wondrous, ghee-rich chariot of you two, ahead of the Usas.

sanskrit: ā nā̍satyā tri̱bhir e̍kāda̱śair i̱ha de̱vebhi̍r yātam madhu̱peya̍m aśvinā | prāyu̱s tāri̍ṣṭa̱ṁ nī rapā̍ṁsi mṛkṣata̱ṁ sedha̍ta̱ṁ dveṣo̱ bhava̍taṁ sacā̱bhuvā̍ ||
english: Come here, O Nāsatyas, with three times eleven gods for the honey-drinking, O Aśvins. Preserve our life uninjured; wipe away our sins; ward off enmity; be ever present.

sanskrit: ā no̍ aśvinā tri̱vṛtā̱ rathe̍nā̱rvāñca̍ṁ ra̱yiṁ va̍hataṁ su̱vīra̍m | śṛ̱ṇvantā̍ vā̱m ava̍se johavīmi vṛ̱dhe ca̍ no bhavata̱ṁ vāja̍sātau ||
english: O Aśvins, bring us on your triple chariot riches turned toward us, [rich] in brave heroes. Hearing [our call] I invoke you two again and again for protection; be for our growth in the conquest of prizes.

sanskrit: hvayā̍my a̱gnim pra̍tha̱maṁ sva̱staye̱ hvayā̍mi mi̱trāvaru̍ṇāv i̱hāva̍se | hvayā̍mi̱ rātrī̱ṁ jaga̍to ni̱veśa̍nī̱ṁ hvayā̍mi de̱vaṁ sa̍vi̱tāra̍m ū̱taye̍ ||
english: I invoke Agni first for well-being; I invoke Mitra and Varuṇa here for aid. I invoke Night, the settler of the world; I invoke the god Savitṛ for protection.

sanskrit: ā kṛ̱ṣṇena̱ raja̍sā̱ varta̍māno nive̱śaya̍nn a̱mṛta̱m martya̍ṁ ca | hi̱ra̱ṇyaye̍na savi̱tā rathe̱nā de̱vo yā̍ti̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ paśya̍n ||
english: Traveling through the dark realm, settling the immortal and the mortal in their places, Savitṛ the god travels through the worlds seeing all on his golden chariot.

sanskrit: yāti̍ de̱vaḥ pra̱vatā̱ yāty u̱dvatā̱ yāti̍ śu̱bhrābhyā̍ṁ yaja̱to hari̍bhyām | ā de̱vo yā̍ti savi̱tā pa̍rā̱vato 'pa̱ viśvā̍ duri̱tā bādha̍mānaḥ ||
english: The god travels on the downward slope, travels on the upward slope, travels with his two bright, adorable bay steeds. The god Savitṛ comes from afar, driving away all difficulties.

sanskrit: a̱bhīvṛ̍ta̱ṁ kṛśa̍nair vi̱śvarū̍pa̱ṁ hira̍ṇyaśamyaṁ yaja̱to bṛ̱hanta̍m | āsthā̱d ratha̍ṁ savi̱tā ci̱trabhā̍nuḥ kṛ̱ṣṇā rajā̍ṁsi̱ tavi̍ṣī̱ṁ dadhā̍naḥ ||
english: Covered with pearls, of all forms, with golden bolts, adorable, and vast — Savitṛ of brilliant radiance has mounted his chariot, bearing strength through the dark realms.

sanskrit: vi janā̍ñ chyā̱vāḥ śi̍ti̱pādo̍ akhya̱n ratha̱ṁ hira̍ṇyapraüga̱ṁ vaha̍ntaḥ | śaśva̱d viśa̍ḥ savi̱tur daivya̍syo̱pasthe̱ viśvā̱ bhuva̍nāni tasthuḥ ||
english: The dark, white-footed [horses] displayed the peoples, drawing the chariot with the golden yoke-pole. All peoples, all worlds have always stood in the lap of divine Savitṛ.

sanskrit: ti̱sro dyāva̍ḥ savi̱tur dvā u̱pasthā̱m̐ ekā̍ ya̱masya̱ bhuva̍ne virā̱ṣāṭ | ā̱ṇiṁ na rathya̍m a̱mṛtādhi̍ tasthur i̱ha bra̍vītu̱ ya u̱ tac cike̍tat ||
english: Three heavens belong to Savitṛ — two are his lap, one belongs in the world of Yama, the all-conquering. Upon the immortal as upon a chariot axle they are established — let him who knows this speak it here.

sanskrit: vi su̍pa̱rṇo a̱ntari̍kṣāṇy akhyad gabhī̱rave̍pā̱ asu̍raḥ sunī̱thaḥ | kve̱3̱̍dānī̱ṁ sūrya̱ḥ kaś ci̍keta kata̱māṁ dyāṁ ra̱śmir a̱syā ta̍tāna ||
english: The fair-winged one [Savitṛ] surveyed the atmospheres, the Asura of deep inspiration and good guidance. Where is the sun now? Who knows it? To which heaven has his ray stretched forth?

sanskrit: a̱ṣṭau vy a̍khyat ka̱kubha̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyās trī dhanva̱ yoja̍nā sa̱pta sindhū̍n | hi̱ra̱ṇyā̱kṣaḥ sa̍vi̱tā de̱va āgā̱d dadha̱d ratnā̍ dā̱śuṣe̱ vāryā̍ṇi ||
english: He surveyed the eight peaks of the earth, the three desert-distances, the seven rivers. Golden-eyed Savitṛ the god has come, granting desirable treasures to the pious worshipper.

sanskrit: hira̍ṇyapāṇiḥ savi̱tā vica̍rṣaṇir u̱bhe dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̱ntar ī̍yate | apāmī̍vā̱m bādha̍te̱ veti̱ sūrya̍m a̱bhi kṛ̱ṣṇena̱ raja̍sā̱ dyām ṛ̍ṇoti ||
english: Golden-handed Savitṛ, all-seeing one, moves between both Heaven and Earth. He drives away disease and goes to meet the sun; he presses the sky downward with the dark realm.

sanskrit: hira̍ṇyahasto̱ asu̍raḥ sunī̱thaḥ su̍mṛḻī̱kaḥ svavā̍m̐ yātv a̱rvāṅ | a̱pa̱sedha̍n ra̱kṣaso̍ yātu̱dhānā̱n asthā̍d de̱vaḥ pra̍tido̱ṣaṁ gṛ̍ṇā̱naḥ ||
english: Golden-handed, the Asura of good guidance, most gracious, self-dependent — may he come here toward us. Repelling demons and sorcerers, the god has stood at evening, receiving praises.

sanskrit: ye te̱ panthā̍ḥ savitaḥ pū̱rvyāso̍ 're̱ṇava̱ḥ sukṛ̍tā a̱ntari̍kṣe | tebhi̍r no a̱dya pa̱thibhi̍ḥ su̱gebhī̱ rakṣā̍ ca no̱ adhi̍ ca brūhi deva ||
english: O Savitṛ, those ancient paths of yours, dustless and well-made in the atmosphere — by those easily traveled paths protect us today and speak over us, O god.

sanskrit: pra vo̍ ya̱hvam pu̍rū̱ṇāṁ vi̱śāṁ de̍vaya̱tīnā̍m | a̱gniṁ sū̱ktebhi̱r vaco̍bhir īmahe̱ yaṁ sī̱m id a̱nya īḻa̍te ||
english: For you many peoples longing for the gods — we approach Agni the young, the great, with well-spoken words and praises; him whom another also implores.

sanskrit: janā̍so a̱gniṁ da̍dhire saho̱vṛdha̍ṁ ha̱viṣma̍nto vidhema te | sa tvaṁ no̍ a̱dya su̱manā̍ i̱hāvi̱tā bhavā̱ vāje̍ṣu santya ||
english: The peoples who possess oblations have established Agni, who grows with might; we would serve you, O truly existent one. Be you today favorably disposed and a helper here to us in contests.

sanskrit: pra tvā̍ dū̱taṁ vṛ̍ṇīmahe̱ hotā̍raṁ vi̱śvave̍dasam | ma̱has te̍ sa̱to vi ca̍ranty a̱rcayo̍ di̱vi spṛ̍śanti bhā̱nava̍ḥ ||
english: We choose you as our messenger, as the priest who calls, the all-knowing. Your flames spread abroad in all directions as you are great; your radiances touch the sky.

sanskrit: de̱vāsa̍s tvā̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā saṁ dū̱tam pra̱tnam i̍ndhate | viśva̱ṁ so a̍gne jayati̱ tvayā̱ dhana̱ṁ yas te̍ da̱dāśa̱ martya̍ḥ ||
english: The gods, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman kindle you, the ancient messenger, together. O Agni, that mortal wins all wealth with you who has pleased you.

sanskrit: ma̱ndro hotā̍ gṛ̱hapa̍ti̱r agne̍ dū̱to vi̱śām a̍si | tve viśvā̱ saṁga̍tāni vra̱tā dhru̱vā yāni̍ de̱vā akṛ̍ṇvata ||
english: O Agni, you are the gladsome Hotṛ, the householder, the messenger of the clans. In you all the fixed ordinances are gathered together which the gods have established.

sanskrit: tve id a̍gne su̱bhage̍ yaviṣṭhya̱ viśva̱m ā hū̍yate ha̱viḥ | sa tvaṁ no̍ a̱dya su̱manā̍ u̱tāpa̱raṁ yakṣi̍ de̱vān su̱vīryā̍ ||
english: In you, O Agni, most blessed, most youthful one, all the oblation is offered. Be well-disposed to us today and again worship the gods for brave heroism.

sanskrit: taṁ ghe̍m i̱tthā na̍ma̱svina̱ upa̍ sva̱rāja̍m āsate | hotrā̍bhir a̱gnim manu̍ṣa̱ḥ sam i̍ndhate titi̱rvāṁso̱ ati̱ sridha̍ḥ ||
english: Thus, bowing in homage, men approach him, the self-king. Men kindle Agni with the Hotṛ-calls, desiring to cross over failures.

sanskrit: ghnanto̍ vṛ̱tram a̍tara̱n roda̍sī a̱pa u̱ru kṣayā̍ya cakrire | bhuva̱t kaṇve̱ vṛṣā̍ dyu̱mny āhu̍ta̱ḥ kranda̱d aśvo̱ gavi̍ṣṭiṣu ||
english: Slaying Vṛtra they crossed Heaven and Earth; they made wide space for dwelling. The bull [Agni], full of brilliance, invoked among the Kaṇvas — the horse will neigh in the cattle raids.

sanskrit: saṁ sī̍dasva ma̱hām̐ a̍si̱ śoca̍sva deva̱vīta̍maḥ | vi dhū̱mam a̍gne aru̱ṣam mi̍yedhya sṛ̱ja pra̍śasta darśa̱tam ||
english: Settle yourself down — you are great; blaze forth, most desired of gods. O Agni, let the ruddy smoke stream forth, splendid one, visible and praiseworthy.

sanskrit: yaṁ tvā̍ de̱vāso̱ mana̍ve da̱dhur i̱ha yaji̍ṣṭhaṁ havyavāhana | yaṁ kaṇvo̱ medhyā̍tithir dhana̱spṛta̱ṁ yaṁ vṛṣā̱ yam u̍pastu̱taḥ ||
english: You whom the gods placed here for Manu, most worthy of worship, O carrier of oblations — you whom Kaṇva, Medhyātithi, Dhanasṛt, Vṛṣā, and Upastuta [have praised].

sanskrit: yam a̱gnim medhyā̍tithi̱ḥ kaṇva̍ ī̱dha ṛ̱tād adhi̍ | tasya̱ preṣo̍ dīdiyu̱s tam i̱mā ṛca̱s tam a̱gniṁ va̍rdhayāmasi ||
english: The Agni which Medhyātithi, the Kaṇva, kindled upon the [altar of] Ṛta — his flames have shone; these hymns magnify that Agni.

sanskrit: rā̱yas pū̍rdhi svadhā̱vo 'sti̱ hi te 'gne̍ de̱veṣv āpya̍m | tvaṁ vāja̍sya̱ śrutya̍sya rājasi̱ sa no̍ mṛḻa ma̱hām̐ a̍si ||
english: Fill [us] with wealth, O self-strong one — for you have something to obtain among the gods, O Agni. You rule over renowned prize. Have mercy on us — you are great.

sanskrit: ū̱rdhva ū̱ ṣu ṇa̍ ū̱taye̱ tiṣṭhā̍ de̱vo na sa̍vi̱tā | ū̱rdhvo vāja̍sya̱ sani̍tā̱ yad a̱ñjibhi̍r vā̱ghadbhi̍r vi̱hvayā̍mahe ||
english: Rise up now for our protection, like the god Savitṛ. Rise up as the winner of the prize when we invoke you with the anointed singers.

sanskrit: ū̱rdhvo na̍ḥ pā̱hy aṁha̍so̱ ni ke̱tunā̱ viśva̱ṁ sam a̱triṇa̍ṁ daha | kṛ̱dhī na̍ ū̱rdhvāñ ca̱rathā̍ya jī̱vase̍ vi̱dā de̱veṣu̍ no̱ duva̍ḥ ||
english: Rising, protect us from distress; burn up all things that devour, with your banner. Make us rise up to wander and to live; find our service among the gods.

sanskrit: pā̱hi no̍ agne ra̱kṣasa̍ḥ pā̱hi dhū̱rter arā̍vṇaḥ | pā̱hi rīṣa̍ta u̱ta vā̱ jighā̍ṁsato̱ bṛha̍dbhāno̱ yavi̍ṣṭhya ||
english: O Agni, protect us from the demon, protect us from the deceitful ungiver. Protect from the injurer and even from him who would slay us, O you of great brilliance, most youthful one.

sanskrit: gha̱neva̱ viṣva̱g vi ja̱hy arā̍vṇa̱s tapu̍rjambha̱ yo a̍sma̱dhruk | yo martya̱ḥ śiśī̍te̱ aty a̱ktubhi̱r mā na̱ḥ sa ri̱pur ī̍śata ||
english: Strike in all directions, like a hammer, those ungiver enemies who harm us, O you with fiery jaws. Let not that mortal enemy who sharpens himself against us in the night hours hold power over us.

sanskrit: a̱gnir va̍vne su̱vīrya̍m a̱gniḥ kaṇvā̍ya̱ saubha̍gam | a̱gniḥ prāva̍n mi̱trota medhyā̍tithim a̱gniḥ sā̱tā u̍pastu̱tam ||
english: Agni has gained [for us] brave heroism; Agni has gained good fortune for the Kaṇva. Agni helped Mitra and also Medhyātithi; Agni in the winning [helped] Upastuta.

sanskrit: a̱gninā̍ tu̱rvaśa̱ṁ yadu̍m parā̱vata̍ u̱grāde̍vaṁ havāmahe | a̱gnir na̍ya̱n nava̍vāstvam bṛ̱hadra̍thaṁ tu̱rvīti̱ṁ dasya̍ve̱ saha̍ḥ ||
english: With Agni we invoke Turvaśa and Yadu from afar, and Ugrādeva. Agni leading Navavāstava [and] Bṛhadratha — Turvīti [received] strength against the Dasyu.

sanskrit: ni tvām a̍gne̱ manu̍r dadhe̱ jyoti̱r janā̍ya̱ śaśva̍te | dī̱detha̱ kaṇva̍ ṛ̱tajā̍ta ukṣi̱to yaṁ na̍ma̱syanti̍ kṛ̱ṣṭaya̍ḥ ||
english: Manu set you down, O Agni, as the light for the people for ever. You shone forth, born of Ṛta, O Kaṇva, when strengthened — you whom all peoples revere.

sanskrit: tve̱ṣāso̍ a̱gner ama̍vanto a̱rcayo̍ bhī̱māso̱ na pratī̍taye | ra̱kṣa̱svina̱ḥ sada̱m id yā̍tu̱māva̍to̱ viśva̱ṁ sam a̱triṇa̍ṁ daha ||
english: Resplendent and mighty are the flames of Agni, terrible to confront. Protective always against sorcerers, burn up everything that devours.

sanskrit: krī̱ḻaṁ va̱ḥ śardho̱ māru̍tam ana̱rvāṇa̍ṁ rathe̱śubha̍m | kaṇvā̍ a̱bhi pra gā̍yata ||
english: O Kaṇvas, sing forth in praise of the sport-loving Marut troop — not to be checked, glorious in their chariot.

sanskrit: ye pṛṣa̍tībhir ṛ̱ṣṭibhi̍ḥ sā̱kaṁ vāśī̍bhir a̱ñjibhi̍ḥ | ajā̍yanta̱ svabhā̍navaḥ ||
english: They who were born with their own radiance, with speckled deer, with spears, together with their axes, and their [ointment-]staves.

sanskrit: i̱heva̍ śṛṇva eṣā̱ṁ kaśā̱ haste̍ṣu̱ yad vadā̍n | ni yāma̍ñ ci̱tram ṛ̍ñjate ||
english: Here, as it were, I hear the whips in their hands, as they speak. Along their course they adorn themselves brilliantly.

sanskrit: pra va̱ḥ śardhā̍ya̱ ghṛṣva̍ye tve̱ṣadyu̍mnāya śu̱ṣmiṇe̍ | de̱vatta̱m brahma̍ gāyata ||
english: Sing for your excited troop, for those of fearful splendor, the vigorous ones — sing the god-given sacred prayer.

sanskrit: pra śa̍ṁsā̱ goṣv aghnya̍ṁ krī̱ḻaṁ yac chardho̱ māru̍tam | jambhe̱ rasa̍sya vāvṛdhe ||
english: Proclaim the inviolable [might] in the cows, the sport of the Marut troop — it has grown strong in the jaws of taste.

sanskrit: ko vo̱ varṣi̍ṣṭha̱ ā na̍ro di̱vaś ca̱ gmaś ca̍ dhūtayaḥ | yat sī̱m anta̱ṁ na dhū̍nu̱tha ||
english: Who among you is the greatest, O men, O shakers of heaven and earth? Since you shake [even] what is at the boundary.

sanskrit: ni vo̱ yāmā̍ya̱ mānu̍ṣo da̱dhra u̱grāya̍ ma̱nyave̍ | jihī̍ta̱ parva̍to gi̱riḥ ||
english: At your onslaught, at your fierce fury, the mountain, the rock trembles for mortal man.

sanskrit: yeṣā̱m ajme̍ṣu pṛthi̱vī ju̍ju̱rvām̐ i̍va vi̱śpati̍ḥ | bhi̱yā yāme̍ṣu̱ reja̍te ||
english: At whose rushing even the earth, like an aged lord of the clan, trembles in fear at their courses.

sanskrit: sthi̱raṁ hi jāna̍m eṣā̱ṁ vayo̍ mā̱tur nire̍tave | yat sī̱m anu̍ dvi̱tā śava̍ḥ ||
english: For strong is their birth, [sprung] from their mother's womb to go forth — when their power follows them as a second force.

sanskrit: ud u̱ tye sū̱navo̱ gira̱ḥ kāṣṭhā̱ ajme̍ṣv atnata | vā̱śrā a̍bhi̱jñu yāta̍ve ||
english: Up have those sons [the Maruts] stretched their shouts like courses at their rushings — like lowing [cows] going knee-deep.

sanskrit: tyaṁ ci̍d ghā dī̱rgham pṛ̱thum mi̱ho napā̍ta̱m amṛ̍dhram | pra cyā̍vayanti̱ yāma̍bhiḥ ||
english: Even that long, broad, irresistible child of mist [i.e. the rain cloud] they cause to rush forward with their courses.

sanskrit: maru̍to̱ yad dha̍ vo̱ bala̱ṁ janā̍m̐ acucyavītana | gi̱rīm̐r a̍cucyavītana ||
english: O Maruts, when with your strength you have caused peoples to tremble, you have caused mountains to tremble.

sanskrit: yad dha̱ yānti̍ ma̱ruta̱ḥ saṁ ha̍ bruva̱te 'dhva̱nn ā | śṛ̱ṇoti̱ kaś ci̍d eṣām ||
english: When the Maruts go forth and speak together on the way — does anyone hear them?

sanskrit: pra yā̍ta̱ śībha̍m ā̱śubhi̱ḥ santi̱ kaṇve̍ṣu vo̱ duva̍ḥ | tatro̱ ṣu mā̍dayādhvai ||
english: Go swiftly with your swift ones — your services are among the Kaṇvas. There indeed rejoice.

sanskrit: asti̱ hi ṣmā̱ madā̍ya va̱ḥ smasi̍ ṣmā va̱yam e̍ṣām | viśva̍ṁ ci̱d āyu̍r jī̱vase̍ ||
english: For there is indeed [something] for your joy, and we are indeed theirs. May we live out our whole lifespan.

sanskrit: kad dha̍ nū̱naṁ ka̍dhapriyaḥ pi̱tā pu̱traṁ na hasta̍yoḥ | da̱dhi̱dhve vṛ̍ktabarhiṣaḥ ||
english: How now, O you whose delight is [in being asked] 'how?' — do you hold [us] in your hands like a father his son? O you for whom the sacred grass has been strewn.

sanskrit: kva̍ nū̱naṁ kad vo̱ artha̱ṁ gantā̍ di̱vo na pṛ̍thi̱vyāḥ | kva̍ vo̱ gāvo̱ na ra̍ṇyanti ||
english: Where now, and to what purpose will you go — as if from the sky to the earth? Where do your cows not delight?

sanskrit: kva̍ vaḥ su̱mnā navyā̍ṁsi̱ maru̍ta̱ḥ kva̍ suvi̱tā | kvo̱3̱̍ viśvā̍ni̱ saubha̍gā ||
english: Where, O Maruts, are your new favors? Where your well-being? Where are all your blessings?

sanskrit: yad yū̱yam pṛ̍śnimātaro̱ martā̍sa̱ḥ syāta̍na | sto̱tā vo̍ a̱mṛta̍ḥ syāt ||
english: If you, O sons of Pṛśni, were mortal men, your praiser would be immortal.

sanskrit: mā vo̍ mṛ̱go na yava̍se jari̱tā bhū̱d ajo̍ṣyaḥ | pa̱thā ya̱masya̍ gā̱d upa̍ ||
english: May your praiser not become like a beast in the pasture, unwanted — may he not go along Yama's path.

sanskrit: mo ṣu ṇa̱ḥ parā̍-parā̱ nirṛ̍tir du̱rhaṇā̍ vadhīt | pa̱dī̱ṣṭa tṛṣṇa̍yā sa̱ha ||
english: Let not Nirṛti, the hard-hitting one, slay us again and again; may she perish with thirst.

sanskrit: sa̱tyaṁ tve̱ṣā ama̍vanto̱ dhanva̍ñ ci̱d ā ru̱driyā̍saḥ | miha̍ṁ kṛṇvanty avā̱tām ||
english: Truly the sons of Rudra are formidable and mighty; even across the desert they make moisture without wind.

sanskrit: vā̱śreva̍ vi̱dyun mi̍māti va̱tsaṁ na mā̱tā si̍ṣakti | yad e̍ṣāṁ vṛ̱ṣṭir asa̍rji ||
english: The lightning bellows like a lowing [cow]; the mother clings to the calf — when their rain was let loose.

sanskrit: divā̍ ci̱t tama̍ḥ kṛṇvanti pa̱rjanye̍nodavā̱hena̍ | yat pṛ̍thi̱vīṁ vyu̱ndanti̍ ||
english: Even by day they make darkness with Parjanya laden with waters, when they flood the earth.

sanskrit: adha̍ sva̱nān ma̱rutā̱ṁ viśva̱m ā sadma̱ pārthi̍vam | are̍janta̱ pra mānu̍ṣāḥ ||
english: Then at the roaring of the Maruts all earthly dwellings shook; men trembled and quaked.

sanskrit: maru̍to vīḻupā̱ṇibhi̍ś ci̱trā rodha̍svatī̱r anu̍ | yā̱tem akhi̍drayāmabhiḥ ||
english: O Maruts, with firm-gripping hands travel along the bright, obstructed [roads], with untiring courses.

sanskrit: sthi̱rā va̍ḥ santu ne̱mayo̱ rathā̱ aśvā̍sa eṣām | susa̍ṁskṛtā a̱bhīśa̍vaḥ ||
english: May your fellies be firm; may their chariots and horses, their reins well-fashioned [be ready].

sanskrit: acchā̍ vadā̱ tanā̍ gi̱rā ja̱rāyai̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍m | a̱gnim mi̱traṁ na da̍rśa̱tam ||
english: Speak with continuous praise toward Brahmaṇaspati, whom one desires to see, like Agni, like Mitra.

sanskrit: mi̱mī̱hi śloka̍m ā̱sye̍ pa̱rjanya̍ iva tatanaḥ | gāya̍ gāya̱tram u̱kthya̍m ||
english: Form the chant in [your] mouth, you who have spread [it] like Parjanya; sing the Gāyatric verse worthy of recitation.

sanskrit: vanda̍sva̱ māru̍taṁ ga̱ṇaṁ tve̱ṣam pa̍na̱syum a̱rkiṇa̍m | a̱sme vṛ̱ddhā a̍sann i̱ha ||
english: Praise the Marut host, formidable, wonderful, provided with songs — may the magnified ones be here with us.

sanskrit: pra yad i̱tthā pa̍rā̱vata̍ḥ śo̱cir na māna̱m asya̍tha | kasya̱ kratvā̍ maruta̱ḥ kasya̱ varpa̍sā̱ kaṁ yā̍tha̱ kaṁ ha̍ dhūtayaḥ ||
english: When, just so, from afar you display your glory like a flame — by whose will, O Maruts? In whose form? To whom do you go? Whom indeed do you shake?

sanskrit: sthi̱rā va̍ḥ sa̱ntv āyu̍dhā parā̱ṇude̍ vī̱ḻū u̱ta pra̍ti̱ṣkabhe̍ | yu̱ṣmāka̍m astu̱ tavi̍ṣī̱ panī̍yasī̱ mā martya̍sya mā̱yina̍ḥ ||
english: May your weapons be firm for driving away [enemies], and strong for withstanding them. May your might be the more wonderful — not that of any deceitful mortal.

sanskrit: parā̍ ha̱ yat sthi̱raṁ ha̱tha naro̍ va̱rtaya̍thā gu̱ru | vi yā̍thana va̱nina̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyā vy āśā̱ḥ parva̍tānām ||
english: When, O heroes, you strike away what is firmly fixed and roll away what is heavy — you cleave through the forests of the earth, through the sides of the mountains.

sanskrit: na̱hi va̱ḥ śatru̍r vivi̱de adhi̱ dyavi̱ na bhūmyā̍ṁ riśādasaḥ | yu̱ṣmāka̍m astu̱ tavi̍ṣī̱ tanā̍ yu̱jā rudrā̍so̱ nū ci̍d ā̱dhṛṣe̍ ||
english: No enemy of yours has been found in the sky above, nor on the earth, O eaters of enemies. May your might, O sons of Rudra, be — with your power as an ally — unconquerable even now.

sanskrit: pra ve̍payanti̱ parva̍tā̱n vi vi̍ñcanti̱ vana̱spatī̍n | pro ā̍rata maruto du̱rmadā̍ iva̱ devā̍sa̱ḥ sarva̍yā vi̱śā ||
english: They cause the mountains to tremble; they split open the lords of the forest. The Maruts have rushed forth, like gods intoxicated, with their whole host.

sanskrit: upo̱ rathe̍ṣu̱ pṛṣa̍tīr ayugdhva̱m praṣṭi̍r vahati̱ rohi̍taḥ ||
english: You have yoked the speckled deer to your chariots; the reddish horse draws as the leader. For your course even the earth cried out; mortal men were afraid.

sanskrit: ā vo̍ ma̱kṣū tanā̍ya̱ kaṁ rudrā̱ avo̍ vṛṇīmahe | gantā̍ nū̱naṁ no 'va̍sā̱ yathā̍ pu̱retthā kaṇvā̍ya bi̱bhyuṣe̍ ||
english: We swiftly choose your protection, O sons of Rudra, for our well-being. Come now to us with aid, as of old you came to the frightened Kaṇva.

sanskrit: yu̱ṣmeṣi̍to maruto̱ martye̍ṣita̱ ā yo no̱ abhva̱ īṣa̍te | vi taṁ yu̍yota̱ śava̍sā̱ vy oja̍sā̱ vi yu̱ṣmākā̍bhir ū̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Sent by you, O Maruts, or sent by mortals — whoever attacks us with monstrous force, drive him away with your might, with your power, with your aids.

sanskrit: asā̍mi̱ hi pra̍yajyava̱ḥ kaṇva̍ṁ da̱da pra̍cetasaḥ | asā̍mibhir maruta̱ ā na̍ ū̱tibhi̱r gantā̍ vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ na vi̱dyuta̍ḥ ||
english: For you are worthy of prior worship, O far-seeing ones; grant [your aid] to Kaṇva with your boundless [gifts]. Come to us, O Maruts, with your boundless aids — like lightning with rain.

sanskrit: asā̱my ojo̍ bibhṛthā sudāna̱vo 'sā̍mi dhūtaya̱ḥ śava̍ḥ ||
english: You carry boundless force, O generous givers; your shaking [imparts] boundless vigor. O Maruts, incensed against the sage-haters, let fly your arrow upon the enemy.

sanskrit: ut ti̍ṣṭha brahmaṇas pate deva̱yanta̍s tvemahe | upa̱ pra ya̍ntu ma̱ruta̍ḥ su̱dāna̍va̱ indra̍ prā̱śūr bha̍vā̱ sacā̍ ||
english: Rise up, O Brahmaṇaspati — we the god-seeking ones implore you. Let the Maruts, the generous givers, approach; O Indra, be swift, be our companion.

sanskrit: tvām id dhi sa̍hasas putra̱ martya̍ upabrū̱te dhane̍ hi̱te | su̱vīrya̍m maruta̱ ā svaśvya̱ṁ dadhī̍ta̱ yo va̍ āca̱ke ||
english: You indeed, O son of strength, the mortal calls upon when stakes are set. He who has desired you — may he obtain from the Maruts brave heroism and fine horses.

sanskrit: praitu̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̱ḥ pra de̱vy e̍tu sū̱nṛtā̍ | acchā̍ vī̱raṁ narya̍m pa̱ṅktirā̍dhasaṁ de̱vā ya̱jñaṁ na̍yantu naḥ ||
english: Let Brahmaṇaspati go forth; let the divine Sūnṛtā go forth. Toward the heroic man of manly might who fulfills fivefold — may the gods lead our sacrifice.

sanskrit: yo vā̱ghate̱ dadā̍ti sū̱nara̱ṁ vasu̱ sa dha̍tte̱ akṣi̍ti̱ śrava̍ḥ | tasmā̱ iḻā̍ṁ su̱vīrā̱m ā ya̍jāmahe su̱pratū̍rtim ane̱hasa̍m ||
english: He who gives the singer noble wealth — he acquires undying fame. For him we worship Iḷā, rich in brave men, swift in aid, faultless.

sanskrit: pra nū̱nam brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̱r mantra̍ṁ vadaty u̱kthya̍m | yasmi̱nn indro̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā de̱vā okā̍ṁsi cakri̱re ||
english: Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati speaks the mantra worthy of recitation — in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, the gods, have made their dwelling places.

sanskrit: tam id vo̍cemā vi̱dathe̍ṣu śa̱mbhuva̱m mantra̍ṁ devā ane̱hasa̍m | i̱māṁ ca̱ vāca̍m prati̱harya̍thā naro̱ viśved vā̱mā vo̍ aśnavat ||
english: That beneficent, faultless mantra, O gods, we would speak at the gatherings. And may you, O heroes, like this speech well — may he [the worshipper] obtain all your good things.

sanskrit: ko de̍va̱yanta̍m aśnava̱j jana̱ṁ ko vṛ̱ktaba̍rhiṣam | pra-pra̍ dā̱śvān pa̱styā̍bhir asthitānta̱rvāva̱t kṣaya̍ṁ dadhe ||
english: Who would reach the god-seeking man? Who the man with strewn sacred grass? The generous giver pressed ever forward with his households from within, establishing [his] dwelling.

sanskrit: upa̍ kṣa̱tram pṛ̍ñcī̱ta hanti̱ rāja̍bhir bha̱ye ci̍t sukṣi̱tiṁ da̍dhe | nāsya̍ va̱rtā na ta̍ru̱tā ma̍hādha̱ne nārbhe̍ asti va̱jriṇa̍ḥ ||
english: He should attach himself to kingly power; he establishes good dwelling even in fear, smiting with kings. There is no turner-back, no overcomer for the vajra-wielder [Indra] in the great contest or the small.
